extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, depositary institutions, and patent office examiners dealing with inventions involving microorganisms/biological material
extracted.subtask_description: National legal and procedural rules governing deposit of microorganisms/biological material in patent applications: when deposit is required, what must be deposited and reported, storage duration, and conditions/restrictions for furnishing samples. Covers multiple jurisdictions' provisions and procedural duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit required when biological material not publicly available and not fully described
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention involves use of biological material/microorganism which is not available to the public and cannot be described in the application in such a manner as to enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention, a sample of the biological material/microorganism must be deposited (i.e., deposit is required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold appears in multiple national provisions (e.g., Norway, Philippines, Portugal, Korea, Moldova). It is the trigger for all deposit obligations: if the material can be adequately described or is publicly available, deposit may not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must include deposit data and deposit details
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall contain the data at the disposal of the applicant relevant to the properties of the microorganism and shall mention the institution with which, the number under which and the date on which the culture of the microorganism has been deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit in Netherlands and echoed in other jurisdictions: include depositary name/address, deposit number, and deposit date in the application/specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must include deposit-related declarations and receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Together with the application shall be submitted a declaration irrevocably giving permission for the furnishing of samples of the deposited culture, a copy of the receipt issued by the depositary institution, and (where applicable) a copy of a specific declaration required by law/regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands example requires an irrevocable permission declaration and a copy of the deposit receipt; other offices may allow the deposit number/receipt to be furnished within a short time limit after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor statement of microorganism properties and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit must be accompanied by a written statement of the depositor containing: (a) a declaration stating the circumstances and properties of the microorganism of interest for cultivation, storage, handling and viability; (b) an indication of the method permitting the checking of the presence of the microorganism; (c) an identification reference and, where possible, the scientific description and proposed taxonomic designation of the microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands (Section 31D) wording. Many offices require characteristics sufficient to identify and handle the deposit; include biochemical, morphological and taxonomic data where available (e.g., Moldova).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted depositary institutions (Budapest Treaty or designated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposit of cultures of microorganisms may be effected with an institution which has acquired the status of international depositary authority under the Budapest Treaty or with an institution designated/approved by the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common rule across jurisdictions: use an international depositary authority under the Budapest Treaty or a nationally designated institution (Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Korea, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of deposit — by the filing date (or prior to filing/priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposit of a microorganism/biological material must be made at the date of filing of the patent application, or, in some jurisdictions, prior to the filing date or the claimed priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most jurisdictions require deposit no later than the filing date (Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Korea, Philippines). Some require proof that deposit was made prior to filing/priority (Moldova). Certain offices permit furnishing of deposit number/receipt within a short post-filing time limit (Netherlands: one month; Norway: notify within 16 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of storage — minimum terms and applicable rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositary institutions shall store deposited microorganisms/biological material for specified minimum periods (e.g., at least 30 years from date of deposit; at least 5 years after most recent request), or in some jurisdictions for the life of the patent plus an additional period, or in accordance with the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Netherlands and Korea require at least 30 years; Korean rules also require 5 years after most recent request; Poland: life of patent plus three years; Portugal: 'in accordance with Budapest Treaty (Rule 9)'; some jurisdictions reference Budapest Treaty default terms when no national provision exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of availability of samples (when samples may be furnished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples become available for furnishing at a specified procedural milestone: e.g., from the date of filing (Netherlands) or from the date of publication/making documents available/the registration of the patent right (Norway, Korea), and remain available until it is certain no patent will be granted or until the patent has lost effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact trigger varies by country (filing date, publication date, making documents available, or registration). The availability period often continues through grant and in some cases after revocation/annulment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement deposit and notification when culture ceases to be available
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deposited culture ceases to be available because it is no longer viable or the institution cannot furnish samples (or the institution discontinues functions or no longer complies with designation), a new deposit must be effected within a prescribed time (e.g., three months or four months) after notification; the new deposit must be accompanied by a statement signed by the depositor that the newly deposited culture is identical to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands: three months after notification; Norway/Moldova: notification and specified time limits (e.g., notify Patent Office and forward new deposit document within four months). Also Patent Office may publish notification in official Journal. New deposit may be deemed to have the original deposit date in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request samples (eligibility to request furnishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who is entitled under the national patent law to inspect the application documents or, in some stages, any requester may request furnishing of a sample; pre-publication access may be limited to specific parties (e.g., the applicant, the Office, persons authorized by the applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility varies by stage: pre-publication access is often narrowly limited; between publication and grant typically open to any requester (subject to undertakings) or limited to an independent expert if applicant so requests; after grant generally open to anyone requesting it, subject to legal/safety prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request must be accompanied by undertaking/declaration and prescribed form
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for furnishing of a sample must be addressed on a form prescribed by the Patent Office and accompanied by a written declaration that the requester undertakes not to make the material available to third parties and to use it exclusively for experiments/research respecting the invention (or other legally required restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Moldova and others require a prescribed form and explicit undertakings; some require the expert to sign the declaration if access is limited to an expert. Declarations remain binding for the specified period (e.g., until either the patent is no longer in force or it becomes certain no patent will be granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may limit furnishing to a designated expert before publication/grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant for a patent may notify the Patent Office that, until grant or until the application is made public, furnishing of samples may only be performed to an expert designated by the requesting person and approved by the applicant; the expert must co-sign required declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural timing and conditions vary: Norway requires such a request to be filed not later than the day before the application becomes public; Netherlands and Portugal have similar provisions. Qualification and approval of experts are specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of derived cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Derived cultures are any cultures preserving the properties of the deposited culture essential for carrying out the invention. Derived cultures are treated similarly for access undertakings, and the commitment not to make material available to third parties does not prevent deposit of a derived culture necessary for patent procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands and Norway define and treat derived cultures explicitly. Undertakings typically apply equally to derived material that retains essential characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office duties: transmission, notification and information duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a request for a sample the Patent Office shall send the request to the depositary institution and shall state whether a patent application containing notification of the deposit has been filed and whether the requester is entitled to be furnished; the Office shall send a copy of the request to the applicant/patent proprietor and notify parties if it refuses to issue a declaration. The Office shall publish notifications where an institution ceases to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands and Norway explicitly set out these transmission and notification duties. Offices may maintain lists of approved experts and may demand receipts as proof of correctness of deposit information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert qualification and designation for restricted access
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'expert' may be (a) any natural person proved on filing the request that the applicant has approved of his designation, or (b) any natural person acknowledged as an expert by the President/Head of the Patent Office; Offices may maintain lists of persons who can be used as experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation procedures and who qualifies differ by country. Norway will draw up a list of persons; the applicant's prior approval may be required in many systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on issuing samples for legal or safety reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample shall not be issued to anyone who by law/regulation is not entitled to handle the deposited material, or whose handling of the sample would be assumed to involve considerable risk due to the harmful properties of the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norway explicitly bars issuance where legal entitlement is lacking or handling poses considerable risk. Other jurisdictions include similar safety/legality exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and formal requirements for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for issuance of samples must be made in writing and, in some jurisdictions, within certain deadlines (e.g., before the application is made public, or the day before public availability); requests must be worded in accordance with implementing regulations (e.g., Rule 11 of the Budapest Treaty implementing regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different Offices set different procedural deadlines (Norway: day before publication; Moldova: before completion of technical preparations for publication). Formal wording requirements are commonly referenced to implementing regulations or national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary institution obligations (access, permanent collection, storage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositary institution must keep the culture in permanent collection or be under contractual obligation to do so and must provide access/provide samples to persons who have interest in matters relating to the published patent application, subject to undertakings and national procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philippines requires depositary to place culture in permanent collection and provide access; Poland names national depositary institutions and states requirements are in conformity with Budapest Treaty. Storage/availability duties often governed by Budapest Treaty or national implementing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when depositor differs from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the biological material has been deposited by a person other than the applicant, a document must be annexed to the patent application evidencing that the depositor has authorized the applicant to refer to the deposited material and consents to its being made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moldova (Implementing Regulations) and similar national provisions require written authorization to avoid disputes over access and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant availability of samples including after revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: After a patent has been granted anyone who requests a sample of the deposited material shall be furnished with a sample, even if the patent has been determined/annulled/revoked (subject to statutory exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norway explicitly provides access after grant even if patent is later annulled; several other jurisdictions similarly permit post-grant access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation after refusal/withdrawal—expert-only period (20 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application is refused or withdrawn, the applicant may request that access to deposited material be limited to an independent expert for a specified period (commonly 20 years from filing date); in such case normal undertakings apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portugal and Moldova explicitly provide for a 20-year expert-only limitation after refusal/withdrawal. Timing for filing such a request is often before publication preparations are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory particulars in deposit certificate/document
rubrics_metrics.description: The document certifying the deposit shall contain the name and address of the recognized collection, the date of deposit (year, month, day), the denomination (name) of the microorganism, the deposit number, and the biochemical, morphological and taxonomic characteristics of the deposited microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moldova lists these particulars explicitly (Implementing Regulations, Rule 156). Other Offices require similar identifying data to ensure correct identification and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of requester undertakings
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester’s undertaking (not to make available to third parties and to use the sample only for experimental purposes) applies until the date on which it has become certain no patent will be granted on the application or, where a patent has been granted, for the period it remains in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netherlands and Moldova make the duration of the undertakings explicit. Undertakings therefore often persist through prosecution until final decision or through patent term if granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication access exceptions and eligible parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to publication of the patent application, samples may be issued only to narrow categories: e.g., at request of the Office (if necessary for the patenting procedure or litigation), to the applicant upon request, to authorities or persons authorized by the applicant, and to any person having the right to inspect the files under the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moldova enumerates pre-publication eligible parties; Portugal and others restrict pre-publication access to authorized persons. Such pre-publication access is typically highly controlled and may require special authorization/undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement on transfers between depositaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If deposited biological material is transferred to another international depositary institution (pursuant to applicable rules), the applicant or patent holder shall notify the Patent Office of the transfer and of the reference number accorded by the new institution; the Office may demand a copy of the receipt as proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norway and other jurisdictions require notification and may request receipt copies. Transfers must comply with Budapest Treaty procedures (e.g., Rule 5(1)).
